But we know that, variance $= \dfrac{∑ x^{2}}{n} - {\left(\dfrac{∑ x}{n}\right)}^{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{134 + x^{2}}{4} - {\left(\dfrac{16 + x}{4}\right)}^{2} = \dfrac{49}{4}$ (given)

$⇒ \left(x - 6\right)\left(3x - 14\right) = 0 ⇒ x = 6, x = \dfrac{14}{3}$
Therefore, the values of $x$ are $6$ or $\dfrac{14}{3}$

questions.solution:
Given, $C{V}_{1} = 60, {CV}_{2} = 75, {\sigma}_{1} = 18$ and ${\sigma}_{2} = 15$
Let ${\overset{-}{x}}_{1}$ and ${\overset{-}{x}}_{2}$ be the means of ${1}^{st}$ and ${2}^{nd}$ distribution respectively.
Then, $C{V}_{1} = \dfrac{{\sigma}_{1}}{{\overset{-}{x}}_{1}} \times 100 ⇒ {\overset{-}{x}}_{1} = \dfrac{18 \times 100}{60} = 30$

questions.q: If the variance of the first $n$ natural numbers is $10$ and the variance of the first $m$ even natural numbers is $16,$ then the value of  $m + n$ is equal to
questions.solution:
$var\left(1, 2, \ldots n\right) = 10 ⇒ \dfrac{{1}^{2} + {2}^{2} + \ldots + {n}^{2}}{n} - {\left(\dfrac{1 + 2 + \ldots + n}{n}\right)}^{2} = 10$
$⇒ \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\left(2n + 1\right)}{6} - {\left(\dfrac{n + 1}{2}\right)}^{2} = 10$
$⇒ {n}^{2} - 1 = 120 ⇒ n = 11$
$var\left(2, 4, 6 \ldots . , 2m\right) = 16 ⇒ var\left(1, 2 \ldots . , m\right) = 4$
$⇒ {m}^{2} - 1 = 48 ⇒ m = 7 ⇒ m + n = 18$

questions.q: In ten observations, the mean of all $10$ numbers is $15$, the mean of the first six observations is $16$ and the mean of the last five observations is $12$. The sixth number is
questions.solution:
Let the mean of the last four observations be ${A}_{2}$. Then, by the formula for combined mean, we get,

$15 = \dfrac{6 \times 16 + 4 \times {A}_{2}}{6 + 4}$

or $150 = 96 + 4{A}_{2}$

$∴ {A}_{2} = \dfrac{54}{4}$

Let the sixth number is $x$, then taking the sixth number as a collection, the combined mean of this collection and the collection of the last four is $12$.

$∴$ By the definition of combined mean

$12 = \dfrac{1 \times x + 4 \times \dfrac{54}{4}}{1 + 4}$

$∴ 60 = x + 54 ∴ x = 6$

Hence, the sixth number $= 6$

questions.solution:
$\begin{cases}{x}_{i} & : & {1}^{2} & {2}^{2} & {3}^{2} & {4}^{2} & . . . & \left(n - 1\right)2 & n^{2} \\ {f}_{i} & : & n & n - 1 & n - 2 & n - 3 & . . . & 2 & 1\end{cases}$
$∴ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i}{f}_{i} = {1}^{2} ⋅ n + {2}^{2}\left(n - 1\right) + {3}^{2}\left(n - 2\right) + . . .+ \left(n - 1\right)2x + n^{2} ⋅ 1$

$= \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)2\left(2n + 1\right)}{6} - \dfrac{n^{2}\left(n + 1\right)2}{4}$

Mean $= \dfrac{Σ{f}_{i}{x}_{i}}{Σ{f}_{i}} = \dfrac{n\left(n + 1\right)2\left(n + 2\right)}{12} \times \dfrac{2}{n\left(n + 1\right)}$

$= \dfrac{\left(n + 1\right)\left(n + 2\right)}{6}$

We have, $\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{ \left({x}_{i} +1\right)}^{2} = 11n \ldots \ldots . \left(i\right)$

Adding $\left(i\right)$ and $\left($ ii\right)$ , we get

$⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_i^{2}}{n} =8$

4\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i} = 4n ⇒ \mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i} = n ⇒ \dfrac{\mathop{∑}_{i = 1}^{n}{x}_{i}}{n} =$$1$
